column1: # markers.tsv — the marker greps from docs/reference/hermes-update-plan-v2026.8.3.md
# §Phase 4, turned into a machine-checkable list.
# Every row is a string that MUST be present in the built image's hermes tree.
# verify-markers.sh greps them all and fails the build if any is missing. This
# is the mechanism that catches, at build time and not on a live tenant:
#   * an upstream release that silently dropped a fix we rely on (the OAuth
#     billing lane — see docs/reference/hermes-400-extra-usage-fix.md); and
#   * a patch that "applied cleanly" into the wrong place after a refactor.
# Format: 4 TAB-separated columns.
#   id       short label used in build/CI output
#   file     path relative to the hermes install root (/opt/hermes)
#   pattern  fixed string (grep -F) that must appear in that file
#   required "required" -> missing is a build failure
#            "optional" -> missing is a warning (use for patches not yet
#                          vendored into this repo, so the image still builds)
# Do not use a regex here on purpose: fixed strings survive reformatting, and
# a marker that quietly stops matching because of an escaping subtlety is worse
# than no marker at all.
# id
# The OAuth wire-name promotion. If this disappears, Claude Max / subscription
# OAuth traffic flips from plan-billing to the extra-usage lane and tenants get
# HTTP 400 "out of extra usage". Update plan §1: "the self-update script's
# verification markers ... are both still valid".
upstream-oauth-wire-name
# The double-underscore MCP tool prefix constant that the promotion writes to.
# A single `mcp_` is the exact token that triggers the extra-usage lane.
upstream-mcp-prefix
# --- UPSTREAM anchors the patches attach to ---------------------------------
# These prove the upstream code our patches hook still EXISTS. They are NOT
# evidence that a patch applied — an unpatched tree satisfies every one of them.
# That distinction matters: these rows catch "upstream refactored the thing we
# depend on", while the post-apply rows below catch "the patch did not land".
# Both are real failure modes and they need separate markers.
# All verified present in the v2026.8.3 tree.
patch-002-anchor
patch-002-anchor-notify
patch-003-anchor
# --- POST-APPLY markers: proof each vendored patch actually landed ----------
# Every string below exists ONLY after its patch is applied, so verify-markers
# — which the Dockerfile runs immediately after apply-patches.sh — becomes a
# genuine check that the overlay took effect, not merely that upstream still
# looks familiar.
# This matters more than usual here: all four patches applied with large line
# OFFSETS against v2026.8.3 (001 +549, 002 +2087, 003 +1620). `patch` found the
# right context and reported no fuzz, but "applied at an offset of 2087 lines"
# is exactly the situation where a human should want independent confirmation
# that the change landed somewhere meaningful.
# All four dry-run and applied cleanly against a real v2026.8.3 checkout on
# 2026-08-08, and every marker below was confirmed present in the result.
# 001 — OAuth system-prompt scrubber (agent/anthropic_adapter.py).
#       TWO markers, because the patch carries two independently load-bearing
#       fixes and losing either silently reintroduces HTTP 400 "out of extra
#       usage" on Claude Max / subscription OAuth:
#   /home/agent              the fingerprint scrub. This is a REPLACEMENT string
#                            ("/home/hermes" -> "/home/agent"), so it cannot
#                            appear in an unpatched tree. It is the exact grep
#                            named in hermes-update-plan-v2026.8.3.md §Phase 4.
#   _promote_bare_tool_refs  the 2026-06-19 "part 2" fix. Per the VPS patches
#                            README, bare compound tool tokens left in system
#                            prompt prose (session_search, skill_manage, …) plus
#                            the MEDIA: marker were themselves sufficient to
#                            trigger the 400 — A/B-proven against a live Max
#                            token. The fingerprint scrub does NOT cover that,
#                            so the first marker passing is not sufficient
#                            evidence that billing is safe.
squire-001-oauth-scrubber
squire-001-bare-tool-promotion
# 002 — cross-chat approval routing (tools/approval.py). Adds the helper that
#       lists sessions with pending approvals.
squire-002-blocking-sessions
# 003 — cross-chat approval session key (gateway/slash_commands.py). Lets
#       `/approve <platform:chat_id>` and `/deny <key>` target the originating
#       session from the home chat. Upstream's own /approve still accepts no
#       session-key argument (update plan §2), so this stays ours to carry.
squire-003-xchat-sessionkey
# 004 — DM read receipts (scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge_helpers.js), added
#       2026-08-04, i.e. AFTER the update plan's "001-003" was written.
#       Upstream forces `participant` into the DM readReceiptKey, making the key
#       look group-shaped; WhatsApp then silently drops the receipt and blue
#       ticks never appear. The fix spreads `participant` only when isGroup.
#       INERT IN THIS IMAGE, carried deliberately. Squire is Telegram-only and
#       prd.md §1 names "no Baileys/unofficial WhatsApp" as an explicit v1
#       non-goal; the upstream image also never runs `npm install` in
#       scripts/whatsapp-bridge, so that bridge has no node_modules and cannot
#       execute here. We carry it anyway so our overlay stays identical to the
#       founder's VPS set — a divergent overlay is how rebases start costing
#       hours. Retire when upstream merges PR #79122.
#       Marked required on purpose: if a future size optimisation strips the
#       WhatsApp bridge from the image, this row fails the build and forces that
#       to be a deliberate decision instead of a silent one.
squire-004-dm-read-receipt
